x: Chas. Walker gave the "A" team a good start with a 10 second lead over the rest of the field but Reg Bolam was forced to give ground and handed over in 4th place.

We sent Chas. Walker off on the first stage to Purley and, although, as we anticipated, Alec Olney gave his club the lead, Chas. put up a fine run by handing over in 2nd place, just beating the Midland champion, C.
With Chas. Walker and Bill Lucas running for us in the two-mile team race, we gained an easy win, with Eric Herbert in fifth place to complete our team.

The senior match saw " Ginger " Holtum win the 100, with " Paddy " Mullen second in the 220, while Jim Heathfield was third in the 440 yards. Jack Brown was second to Johnny Prince of S.L.H. in the half-mile, with Bob Taylor third, and Chas.

… with Jack on his heels, they had to give best down the straight, to eventually finish third and fourth. The 1 mile saw Chas. Walker and Bill Lucas both run well, with the former beating Alec Olney for first place, with Bill third.…
Chas. Walker was third in the 1 mile and Bill Lucas occupied a similar place in the 3 miles.
…oints which was our lot this time. Len Herbert and Bill Lucas, in the 3 miles, were responsible for some of these, plus Chas. Walker's sixth place in the 1 mile event.…

Pirie, both just out of the junior stage, and he beat such men as Burfitt, Olney and Jimmy Wood. We also had Chas Walker and Ray Tooby qualifying for the final of this event and this speaks well for our strength at this distance.
At the Inter-Counties meeting we had Harry Churcher gaining 2nd place in the 2 miles walk and Chas. Walker was 6th in the 1 mile and so they both helped towards Surrey retaining their team title.

…am performance was in the 4 x 1 mile for the " Victory Trophy " and our team of Ray Tooby, John Bromley, Bill Lucas and Charles Walker finished a good second to the Poly and beat such clubs as Walton A.C., who had Nankeville running their final " leg," Cambridge H., South London H., Herne Hill H., S…

The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas.
In the 100 yards we had " Ginger " Holtum second and Alan Sexton third, while Chas. Walker was third in the 1 mile, and then Len Herbert was first home in the 2 miles run.
In the 1 mile match we saw Chas. Walker running as second string for London and right well did he do this when he beat the Swedish second string in an inches finish for third place.

The rest of our team managed to keep in front, although Chas. Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.
Chas Walker ran a good race on the next stage to take us up into 2nd place and was only 1 second slower that Morley of Blackheath who were still in the lead.

Chas Walker, although suffering from the after-effects of a cold, ran a good first "leg" which was inside the previous lap record time, held by Bill Lucas, but even so could only hand over in second place to Cook, of Hadleigh A.C.
Charlie Walker won the individual race beating Alec Olney and Ted Manley with Bill Lucas in 4th place, Ray Tooby 7th and Archie Bedford 8th.
This was the second race promoted by the L.C.C. and once again Charlie Walker was first man home, although given a close race by R.

The holder, Chas. Walker, ran a fine race to retain his hold on the Shield although Jack Braughton gave him a close race, and a good sign was the fact that our first six men were all home within 42 seconds.
Chas. Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th.
Pirie and also running in their team were J. Braughton 29th, Bill Lucas 44th, Eddie Short 53rd, Chas.

A good field of 38 runners faced the starter on a snow covered course of two laps, and at the half-distance Charlie Walker was out in front being about 60 yards ahead of Bill Lucas and Jack Brown who were together.
Alec Olney was first home followed by Charlie Walker, and then came Ray Tooby, Eddie Short and Archie Bedford who ran in together, just in front of A.
On the second lap we saw Charlie Walker, Eddie Short, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford running well together with Bill Lucas, our captain, acting as the whipper-in.
Charlie Walker was well up to start with but then seemed to ease off with the result that at the end of the first short lap we had no one in the first fifty placings.
Hudson 6th, Len Adams 5th, Eric Herbert 6th, Len Herbert 4th, Len Bishop 4th, with Eddie Short taking us into the lead on the 9th stage, for Chas.

Badiali was 3rd in the 440 and Jack Brown finished 2nd in the 880 yards with Bob Taylor in 4th place. Bill Lucas and Chas. Walker were 3rd and 4th in the 1 mile, but Len Adams scored a good win when he came home first in the 2 miles run.

…ell to finish 5th and was clocked to do 8 min. 33 secs., which was very fast running. Our other runners were Len Adams, Chas. Walker and Bill Lucas, and we were placed 3rd in the team race to S.L.H., and the Polytechnic H.…
Don Maclean again showed fine form when he ran away from his field in the 1 mile and he clocked 4 min. 22.4 secs., with Chas. Walker in 4th place to help our points total along.
In the 1 mile we had Ray Tooby and Chas. Walker, and Ray found one too good for him in Lloyd-Morgan, the Oxford runner, who won in the good time of 4 min. 19 secs.
Arthur Bruce pulled us up three places on the 2nd stage and Chas. Walker brought us to 5th on the third leg, and we then ran Jack Braughton in an endeavour to overhaul the leaders.

Chas. Walker went off next, and although he did 7th fastest time for this relay he lost 32 seconds, so that at the next change-over we were only a second in front of Essex Beagles with Walton in third place.
Ellis of Maidenhead showed the way in the early stages with Chas. Walker going up to him but before very long Jack Brown and Ray Tooby had taken command.

Finchley H. were second, with the "Bels." in third place, the same position as last year, and whereas Chas. Walker had won the individual race for the past two seasons, this time he could only finish in 21st place.

In mentioning the above names we are not attempting to detract from Jack Brown's running in winning the race, as his time was well up to standard and he finished in comfortable fashion in front of Chas.

On 20th December, against the local club, Cambridge Harriers, it was unfortunate that our captain, Jack Brown, turned up just too late to take part in the race. Holden, of Cambridge, was first home, followed by Chas.

Chas. Walker was our first man home in 5th position, then came Bill Lucas, 12th, and Bill only came into the team in order to make up the number, as he says he has retired from serious competition and declined an invitation to run in the Inter-Counties race.

Then came Denis Brickwood 30th, and as Denis was placed 22nd in the 1939 race, we think it a remarkable achievement for him to drop only eight places after a lapse of 14 years, and just shows what can be done with properly applied training methods. Eddie Short and John Burr also ran quite well, and…

Chas. Walker was 85th and, seeing that he was running in borrowed “togs,” owing to leaving his running kit on a bus on his way to catch the Club coach at Tooting, he can be said to have run reasonably well.

We extend congratulations to Chas. Walker on once again being selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties c.c. race, also to Bob Belmore, who is a second-claim member, and to Jack Brown, who was a scoring member of the Kent team, who were third in the team championship.
Chas. Walker put in a really fine run to put them in the lead on the 3rd stage, and this was maintained by Wright, Short, Lucas and Bedford down to the end of the 7th relay.
The winner was Ray Tooby in a new record time for our 5 miles road course, and Peter Bagnall and Chas. Walker were also both inside the previous record.
Chas. Walker did our fastest time and only just failed by 1 second to gain an award given for the three fastest laps, which all went to members of the home club.
Chas. Walker did 27.01 for 5th fastest time on the 4th stage, which was well behind Arthur Bruce's record for this leg, and his time was beaten by Dalton, of Birchfield, to set up a new record.
In the Senior 880 yards we saw John Bromley score rather a surprise win in the good time of 2 mins. 0.8 sec., with Ian Badiali second and Chas.

Dicky also won the 440 yds., beating Ian Badiali, and Jim Heathfield was 3rd in the 880, with Don Maclean 2nd in the 1 mile in 4 mins. 26.9 secs. Chas. Walker was first home in the 2 mile run in 9 mins. 42.6 secs., with Archie Bedford in second place, and T.

The following evening, at Motspur Park, we fielded a team in a 1 mile medley relay and Ian Badiali gave us the lead over the half-mile stage, then Ian Forrester and Dicky Bartlett did the two 220's with "Jock" Cameron running the quarter, and we eventually finished 3rd. We also turned out a team for…

"Jock" Cameron was 2nd in 51.2 secs., and Jack Brown won the 880, with Frank Wright in 2nd place in 1 min. 59.4 secs. Peter Bagnall was 2nd to Nankeville in a 4 mins. 15 secs 1 mile. and Chas. Walker won the 3 miles in 14 mins. 46.4 secs.
Coxon by inches in 50.5 secs., with Chas.
In the 3 miles we had Chas. Walker and John Burr, and although Chas. took the lead early on, once Gordon Pirie had gone by him he dropped back to finish outside the first six.

The race of the evening was the 4 x 1 mile event for the "Victory Trophy," and on the first leg we saw Jack Brown give us the lead. Chas. Walker ran well to retain this after dropping back at one stage and we then had John Burr doing the third leg.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 59.1 secs., but nearly lost the race by easing at the tape, and Chas. Walker ran well to win the 1 mile in the good time of 4 mins. 22 secs.
In the 1 mile event we saw Willie Nankeville out to do a fast time, which, with the aid of a couple of pace-makers, he duly accomplished—4 mins. 9.4 secs.—and Chas.
Peter Bagnall and Chas. Walker also competed, but here again, with the slowest heat showing 4 mins. 17.8 secs., neither of them could gain a place in the final.

Owing to Len Herbert crying off with a leg injury, plus the fact that the Civil Service meeting took away Jack Brown, Bob Taylor and Chas. Walker, and Ray Tooby was competing at the Inter-Banks, we were unable to field a team in the 2 miles team race.

The " big " event of the meeting was the Club 3 mile track championship, and the holder, Jack Brown, retained his title in 14 mins. 31.4 secs. Chas. Walker, who had made the pace in the early stages of the race, was second, with Bill Lucas, still retired, in third place.

Jack Brown came over from the White City where he had been running for the Great Britain " B " team in the attack on the 4 x 1 mile world's record, and he successfully defended his 1 mile title, beating Chas.
At the " Sward " Trophy meeting at Chiswick we had entered a team for the 2 miles team race, but only Chas. Walker put in an appearance, and he ran as an individual and was second to P.

Chas Walker dropped a place on the long 7th relay but Len Bishop who ran very well, took us back into 2nd place on the 8th leg.Eddie Short and Bob Taylor maintained this position on the two final stages and were unable to overtake the leaders Essex Beagles, who returned a time of 3 hours 49 mins,16secs. to our 3.50.33.

This was held at Wimbledon on October 24th jointly with a match against Herne Hill H. and Sutton and Cheam Harriers. Maynard, Clark and Heywood were the first three home, followed by Chas, Walker and P.

…he holder Jack Brown, made sure of retaining the trophy by scoring a runaway victory in the fast time of 55mins. 9secs. Chas.Walker 55.02 was 2nd with Jim Masters 3rd in 55.17, the next three placings being P.Bagnall 55.40,D.Brickwood 55.56, and E.…

However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front.

Although we did not expect anything brilliant from our runners, they did not run too badly and certainly bettered their "Southern" performance In coming 31st, Chas Walker certainly pulled one out of the bag and so becomes holder of the "Harry Parker" Memorial Trophy, for the ensuing year.

This saw us as usual at three different venues on the same afternoon the first being at Maidenhead where, in the local 10 miles we provided the winner in Chas Walker in 54m. 57s and who was fairly well backed up by Stan Gawler 6th in 56.35 and E.

Charlie Walker performed quite creditably on the first leg to give us third place. John Bromley kept this place on the run to Mitcham although having to give way to Herne Hill who moved up into 2nd place.
Charlie Walker again refused to cane himself over the last mile and was content with 4th. Following him were Tooby, Bedford, Burr, Trower, Brickwood, L.

Charlie Walker was running well to come 3rd and Cliff Roffey 4th. John Burr 5th, gave us a good start. 6th was Johnny Butley, first man home for Surrey A.C. and then four more Bels., Masters, Tooby Trower and Bagnall.
Charlie Walker came in next and so won the Blackstaffe Shield but he only just held off Braughton in the straight. Jumbo Masters came next and Jack Brown only got 3rd Championship medal this year.
After the 27 minute whistle had gone, no further change over was allowed and Charlie Walker, paired with Gordon Biscoe, appeared to be caught napping, Gordon being caught in possession of the baton.

Jack Brown's performance was a little disappointing, but Charlie Walker had obviously recovered from his cold on the "Club" 10 day. Bedford ran a good race and again was seen making his way through the field as the race progressed.

At about 2½ miles Cliff was still leading our team and lying about 60th, Pete Bagnall was next, 83rd with Eddie Patterson 85th, next J. Masters 96th, Dave Baulch 118th, Charlie Walker 120th, Eric Gebbett about 150th, and Jack Brown about 160th.

At the start we found Chas Walker up with the leaders and we were hoping that he could maintain his position for some of the more experienced road men were not running true to form, but his inexperience told in the end and he felt glad to finish.
Chas. Walker ran the first leg (880) and handed the baton to Frank Kemp just in front of T.V.H.

Chas Walker, unpredictable as ever, was 6th just in front of junior George Flanagan whose forward running was a surprise to many. Eric Gebbett was a deserving winner of the handicap with Ron Mitchell and Dave Hooper 2nd and 3rd respectively.
Chas Walker is believed to have done the fastest actual time with a fine 14.49 effort which reduced the course record by a considerable margin and was a vast improvement on his form of a week before.
At this stage we were 1 min. 35 secs. down on the leaders Herne Hill. Chas. Walker was our next performer and despite being overtaken by Cameron of T.V.H., pulled us up to fifth place.

Pete Bagnall finished second, only four seconds behind the Herne Hill International, Mike Maynard. Our next three in were Chas. Walker, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford who filled 4th, 7th and 9th positions respectively.
Charlie Walker suffering from the effects of a cold, hung on well to finish three places behind Peter in 63rd position, with Dave Baulch, 72nd showing some of his previous form.

The Club had nine starters in the Senior Race, compared with 15 last year. Chas. Walker, Jack Braughton, and Archie Bedford were among the non-starters and of those who were running only two were in full training.

Speculation ran high as to whether Charlie Walker could pull the fat out of the fire on the last circuit but unfortunately it was one of those days when Charlie becomes a frustating enigma to his supporters.

Charlie Walker took the lead quickly, with Baulch, Bagnall and Flanagan on his heels. Round the first lap of the Common, Flanagan went to the front but was not allowed to keep his nose ahead for long.

Charlie Walker should have made capital out of his position for the field were spread out ahead of him and although passing Poly. and Manchester, he was caught by Birchfield and Essex Beagles and in the end handed over 12th, 2min. 19 secs, behind Herne Hill who had gone into the lead.
With Charlie Walker 9th and Colin Collis 11th we would have walked away with the team award, but as it was we were 2nd to Ealing Freddie being our third man in 38th position.
We are already London County Cross-Country Champions and we are pleased to see the great form of Jack Brown, Charlie Walker and Charlie Dabbs.
Bob Taylor tried to contact Charlie Walker but failed. However, after much persuasion Bill Bird made our three in the 3000 metres team race, but not being at his best he finished well down.

Charlie Walker and Eric Gebbett ran extremely well. to finish 12th and 13th - Charlie is returning to something like his best form. However, we had to go back to 30th position for our fourth scoring man, Dave Baulch, and consequently we were 3rd team with 47 points behind St.

At the foot of Dale Hill,Charlie Walker waited,as usual, wasting much energy asking all and sundry," what do you think?" Would Charlie pull one out of the bag and put us back in the running for 2nd place?
He was well supported by Chas. Walker, who incidentally, was ill just before the race, in 10th. place, Ray Tooby 11th. and Charlie Dabbs 17th.

Jack Brown ran very impressively to win by a full minute from Charlie Walker with Ray Tooby half a minute further back in third place. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap.

The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.

The race itself, run in very pleasant weather, resolved into a dual between a Belgrave pair, Charlie Walker and C. Henn, and two Hercules runners, who together with four others had been invited to compete.

Then came Chas. Walker, Pete Bagnall, Dave Baulch and Eric Gebbett, all running strongly and all four within reach of one another but unable apparently to join forces, a fact which probably cost us second team place.

There our men showed that at least they could hold on to their positions, and after 3 miles Jack had moved up to the twenties, Eric was running extremely well, just outside the hundred; Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Chas Walker and Len Bishop were our scoring team in that order.
Chas Walker ambled round and we finished 2nd to Thames Valley with Herne Hill 3rd.
Ray Tooby moved up to 4th place on the next stage, and Chas Walker, with an almost identical time, ensured that our next man, Jack Brown, was within striking distance of the leaders.
In Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Pat Newell and Brian Hallowell, to name but a few, we have runners of the class of which champions are made.
At 5 miles Jack Brown had "lost" the field and looked set for another easy win, Colin Collis followed in 5th position from Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop.
Fortunately S.L.H. and T.V.H. were also in the dumps. 2nd Charlie Walker Conditions perfect for a fast run with twelve teams ahead strung out at regular intervals.
Chas Walker was placed third in the Civil Service 5 miles cross-country championship and Dave Baulch was eighth. Bob Plummer, now recovered from his knee trouble plans a full season for 1958.

Charlie Walker, however, was spurred on by the responsibility thrown on his shoulders and set out to recover some of the lost ground. By excellent running he passed team after team and the encouraging cheers of the few supporters on this leg kept him at his task.

The most notable club performer was Charlie Walker who, in finishing seventh in 52m.42s., seems to be returning to his very best form. Our team achieved quite a creditable fifth position which was only six points behind that of the second team.
For the record book, Eric Gebbett excelled over the distance and the extra two miles enabled him to move away from Chas. Walker and finish third to Haslam of T.V.H. and Thornton of Leeds.

Charlie Walker was soon in the first bunch which was headed by Hugh Foord of Brighton and when seen again at the end of the first lap had established himself in second place some distance behimd Foord.

In the absence of Charlie Walker and George Flanagan, the result of this race was very much a matter for speculation. A field of 37 started, including three Essex Beagles men, and a bunch of about twelve runners was soon detached on the first lap, with Eric Gebbett in close attendance.

Eric Gebbett eventually finished 20th after having been up to 15th at one stage - it seems strange to have to report that the extra distance was his downfall.Charlie Walker in 33rd place was very disappointing - perhaps he should not forecast his running before the race - it always seems to be fatal.
This year's race,held on a cold damp day, ran true to form with Charlie Walker, who always performs so well over our own courses, the winner by the comfortable margin of 47 seconds.
Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th.
Next man was Charlie Walker, 77th, an improvement on recent form, with ever consistant Eric Gebbett 134th. A special mention must be made of Clive Shippen who has been short of training.
Eric Gebbett was, as usual, quickly in the lead and he, together with Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch, took the field along at a very brisk pace.
Particularly would I like to see more support from our two and three milers. This year we have missed the assistance of Chas. Walker, Dave Baulch, Brian Hallowell and others.

Dave dropped back at the approach to the first hill and Malcolm likewise at the turn into the second; the remaining three staying together until approximately 400 yds. to go when Clive Shippen sprinted ahead to gain second place, 25 yds. ahead of Charlie Walker, with Eric a further 35 yds. down.

Then satisfied that Brian knew what he was doing, we sped on to Clapham Common for the first change-over. Brian had moved up to seventh and away went Charlie Walker. Portsmouth had a slight lead from Brighton and T.V.H.
Our six were Bob Glover, Malcolm Robinson, Alan Black, Eric Gebbett, Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch; three relative newcomers to road relay racing and three "veterans".

A steady start meant a large bunch of runners in the lead for the first two miles, but as the weaker flesh fell away it was left to Chas. Walker, John Moore and Pat Newell to decide the issue, with Eric Gebbett, Malcolm Robinson and Alan Black forming the spearhead of the second bunch.

Dave Baulch and Chas. Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.

Charlie Walker, Eric Gebbett and Dave Baulch were labouring around the hundred mark. At two miles, with Maynard(H.H.H.) leading from Eldon and Knight, Pat was 15th, John 46th and our sixth scoring man in the nineties.
Charlie Walker, on the eighth stage, was also disappointing with 18.49 and dropped us back to fourth after a battle royal over the last half-mile with Alan Perkins(Ilford) and Bert Ingles (T.V.H.).
John had been allocated the first leg and this was given to Charlie Walker who could not, this year, impress the selectors sufficiently to gain more than the first reserve designation.

Charlie Walker and John Moore did well to take 8th and 10th places respectively. The first major cross-country race, the South of the Thames Junior, was held at Epsom Downs on November 8th and Ken Miller(20th), John Moore(26th), Malcolm Robinson(34th) and Clive Shippen(35th) ran well to give us 3rd…

But Rangit was not to be beaten and they crossed the line to-gether, with a time of 14:52.5, a personal best for each. Don Maclean and Charlie Walker finished 6th & 7th, for the team to take the team award.

Charlie Walker took our first leg but could do no better than finish tenth with a deficit of 58secs. from Surrey A.C. Charlie Dabbs returning to racing of this type after a long series of injuries ran an exceptionally good leg to take us up to third place, only 22secs behind the leaders.
Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot.

Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman.
Charlie Walker (26.22). No lack of experience here although everyone crosses their fingers when 'What do you think' Charlie sets off.

Eric Gebbett was with the leaders for most of the way and despite a lack of finishing speed was a creditable ninth; giving Charlie Walker a wonderful start with five men ideally placed for "picking off" in the 150 yards ahead.

After the half-way mark and turn for home, and two miles of down hill running to go, Brian Hallowell made full use of his long stride to improve his position in the nineties while John Moore and Chas Walker were leading him slightly.

When the race was again seen after 2½ miles, Newell and Dabbs were close together in seventh and ninth places, closely followed by Chas. Walker, in 12th spot, with John Moore a few yards further back, 18th.

CHARLIE WALKER, affectionately known as " What do you think" Charlie, after his habit of enquiring after our chances at all stages of a race, has always been one of our top athletes since joining us in 1948.
The field of thirty-three, minus the title holder Chas. Walker, who was injured, was led by Ron Linstead who set up a lead of some thirty yards by the half-mile.
The first was cross-country captain Clive Shippen in 39th place, with Eric Gebbett nearby 42nd. Then Chas. Walker 50th, Eddie Short 55th and Mal Robinson way back 67th.

Charlie Dabbs notched up his second title of the season when he easily won the Club "Macher Shield" from Charlie Walker. A field of 28 lined up for the start and within half a mile Dabbs, Walker, Newell and David Jones were running together, 35 yards clear of the field.
Showing something like his old form Chas. Walker at 59th was our first man home in the Southern Championships, held at Parliament Hill Fields.

"Dippy Richards of Polytechnic Harriers ran home a clear winner from Mike Maynard (2nd claim to Poly) in this triangular match at Wimbledon. Charlie Dabbs and Chas. Walker both ran soundly for the Bels. and were backed up sufficiently well enough for us to win the match.

The leaders set off at a fast pace with our team placed in the front half of the 600 odd runners. At the end of the first lap Charlie Dabbs and Chas. Walker lay in the 80's with David Jones and Eric Gebbett together 60 places back.
Charlie Walker, once again beginning to show his old form, swept into the lead; only to be passed by Haith of T.V.H. who had moved up from 13th.
Charlie Walker who was third put up a personal best. What a pity Pat Newell, who was working, could not have joined in the fray—who knows what might have happened!

Charlie Walker has probably had a better season than for some years and was in a confident mood and we looked for more gains. Our greatest enigma however was not at his best and when Mick Firth of S.L.H. swept past him without even a challenge we wondered what would happen.

Ted Smith, Hugh McGreechan and Charlie Walker are the proud fathers of newly born sons, whilst John Keown and Eric Gebbett and Jumbo Masters are equally proud of their daughters---perhaps we'll have a ladies section yet !
Chas Walker with a personal best, replaced Ponders End for second place, whilst Dick Shackleford, although dropping to fifteenth, turned in a surprising 14:19 for the 'B'.
John Thresher set the pace with Charlie Walker for 2 miles but decided that two laps of the common was far enough and left Charlie to hold the baby!

Charlie Walker set off on the second leg in great style with Eddie Ellis of TVH breathing down his neck. These two battled throughout and soon disposed of Walton, Blackheath and Highgate but Ealing represented by Blagrove, Brighton with Briault, and Woodford with Chapman were making faster progress…
We hope to see Charlie Walker out again in the New Year. The tragic loss of his 4 year old daughter in October has naturally curtailed his activities.

The strength of every team is governed by its weakest man, but with experienced men like Charlie Walker, John Davies and Eric Gebbett to complete our teams it is difficult to see where our weakest link can lie.

Chas. Walker, vociferous before the start, revised his views after sampling the fast start and finished 100th, just ahead of Ken Miller (116), whilst Eric Gebbett (136) finished two places ahead of our recent county "vest" (!) Mal Robinson.

Charlie Walker took the second leg and in doing 18.25 improved to 9th place - a good solid effort. We were then 42 seconds down on Polytechnic, who had gone into the lead by virtue of an excellent run by B.
Ron must indeed have been pleased to see Charlie Walker waiting for him at the foot of Dale Hill. STAGE 11 - Charlie Walker (20.54, 5th fastest).
In the earlier stages Charlie Walker remained in close contact with the two leaders but gradually he was made to yield ground and left to make certain of third place.
Eric Gebbett ran his usual reliable first stage, keeping us in contact with the leaders and Charlie Walker consolidated this by moving us up to 3rd position.
STAGE 10 - Charlie Walker (21:09. 5th fastest) Chas. gave a little on T.V.H. and Mitcham, but the gap was far too great to give the supporters any hope that we would finish higher than sixth.
A good start, and a strong finish, however gave him the good time of 10:19 and Charlie Walker a line of nine runners all handily placed for "picking off".
In a 10 - mile paarlauf held at Hurlingham on November 26th, Bill Kerr and Charlie Walker finished second to London University pair, recording 45 mins - 38 secs.
Fortunately this alone did not quite decide the result. Charlie Walker and John Davies backed up well, with 6 to score we would have won.

After the first 500 yds of this 3 lap course, Charlie Walker, showing something like his old form, shot into the lead and opened up a gap of 20 yds., hotly pursued by Shippen, Miller, Thresher and our ever-improving junior Tony Fairclough.
Lastly, about next season, I hope we shall see more of Eric Gebbett and Charlie Walker in the lesser road races. Forthcoming attractions:- Mitcham '15', Wigmore '15', and Finchley '20'.

His final position of eleventh gained him a place as reserve for the Inter-Counties and a county vest would be a fitting reward for all Clive's endeavours. Chas. Walker, John Thresher and Ron Linstead supported well but we had to wait some 20 places before Charlie Dabbs and Ken Miller appeared.
Our three 'A' team runners in this event Barry Sawyer, Chas. Walker and Bill Kerr had a most successful afternoon's competition.

Ron Linstead had built up a useful lead over a limping Barry Sawyer who, in turn, was a comfortable distance ahead of Charlie Walker. David Jones, making a welcome return to the running scene was 9th and John Moore, also fighting his way back, 10th.

The experienced element has been, and will be for a while yet, provided by Ron Linstead and Charlie Walker. Ron and Chas. supported almost every one of our winter fixtures and can be relied upon to do likewise next year.
